title: Inside the first EU Culture Dialogue. Will national governments step up?
content:
On 12 November 2026, the first EU Culture Dialogue took place in Brussels hosted by Commissioner Glenn Micallef. The day was full of important announcements from the Commission, lively discussions among 60 representatives of cultural organisations and a bit of planning for the future of EU cultural policy amidst ongoing political drama. Culture Action Europe was represented by Lars Ebert in the morning and Luiza Moroz in the afternoon. Stay with us for this long read as we unpack what happened, what was said and, most importantly, what we made of it all at the end.  

The structured dialogue is a way for the European Commission and the cultural sector to stay in touch and, hopefully, co-create cultural policies together. It gives cultural organisations, networks, and artists a regular opportunity to bring their experience to the Commission, discuss what it is proposing and help decide what should be on the agenda.
